foods.name: Drumstick / Moringa Leaves
synergies: High in natural Vitamin C which boosts plant non-heme iron absorption significantly.
foods.tip: Add a handful to daily dal (pappu) or stir-fry as a dry sabzi with minimal oil.

foods.name: Spinach
synergies: Contains oxalates that bind calcium and iron. Squeezing fresh lemon juice (Vitamin C) breaks inhibition.
foods.tip: Steam or sauté lightly; pair with tomatoes or lemon juice rather than heavy cream/dairy.

foods.name: Fenugreek Leaves
synergies: Rich in both calcium and iron with moderate Vitamin C to aid uptake.
foods.tip: Incorporate into multigrain theplas, stir-fries, or dal.

foods.name: Amaranth Leaves / Chaulai
synergies: One of the most iron-dense traditional Indian greens.
foods.tip: Cook with garlic and mustard seeds as a quick side sabzi.

foods.name: Curry Leaves
synergies: Don't discard them on the plate: chew or powder into podi for maximum iron and calcium extraction.
foods.tip: Blend into chutneys, dry gun powders (karam podi), or herbal decoctions.

foods.name: Finger Millet / Ragi
synergies: Highest calcium density among Indian cereal grains; naturally gluten-free.
foods.tip: Consume as ragi mudde, malt/porridge, or combine with jowar for soft rotis.

foods.name: Pearl Millet / Bajra
synergies: Superb iron-rich gluten-free grain, especially when paired with amla or lemon.
foods.tip: Make winter bajra rotis or bajra khichdi with moong dal and vegetables.

foods.name: White / Black Sesame Seeds
synergies: Calcium powerhouse for vegans with healthy fats that assist fat-soluble nutrient uptake.
foods.tip: Add til laddu with jaggery, sprinkle on rotis, or use in Andhra-style nuvvula podi.

foods.name: Garden Cress Seeds / Halim
synergies: Unmatched iron density (10mg in a single tablespoon!).
foods.tip: Soak 1 tsp in lemon water or tender coconut water for 30 minutes before drinking.

foods.name: Pumpkin Seeds
synergies: Rich in zinc and magnesium alongside iron.
foods.tip: Dry roast and eat as an evening snack.

foods.name: Roasted Bengal Gram
synergies: High fiber and folate. Convenient ready-to-eat office/travel snack.
foods.tip: Pair with a slice of jaggery (chana-gur combination) or toss into chaat with tomatoes.

foods.name: Kidney Beans / Rajma
synergies: High folate and non-heme iron. Soaking overnight neutralizes phytates.
foods.tip: Cook with tomato and ginger-garlic gravy for enhanced taste and acidity to support absorption.

foods.name: Bengal Gram Dal
synergies: Excellent plant protein and folate source.
foods.tip: Prepare as dal tadka or mix with leafy greens like palak or bottle gourd (lauki).

foods.name: Whole Black Gram
synergies: High calcium and folate among whole lentils.
foods.tip: Use in fermented idli/dosa batters or slow-cooked dal makhani (light on cream).

foods.name: Indian Cottage Cheese / Paneer
synergies: High bioavailable dairy calcium and moderate natural B12 for vegetarians.
foods.tip: Consume raw, grilled, or gently tossed in curries.

foods.name: Plain Curd / Dahi
synergies: Probiotics enhance general intestinal nutrient assimilation.
foods.tip: Have with lunch as plain curd, raita, or buttermilk (chaas).

foods.name: Cow's Milk (Boiled)
synergies: Key source of bioavailable B12 and calcium in traditional Indian lacto-vegetarian diets.
foods.tip: Drink warm at night with a pinch of turmeric and black pepper.

foods.name: Boiled Chicken Egg (Whole)
synergies: Yolk contains bioavailable Vitamin D3 and natural Vitamin B12.
foods.tip: Consume the whole egg (including yolk) to get fat-soluble Vitamin D.

foods.name: Skinless Chicken Breast
synergies: Lean heme iron with superior bioavailability over plant sources.
foods.tip: Tikka style, tandoori, or curry with light spices.

foods.name: Chicken Liver
synergies: One of nature's densest sources of heme iron, Vitamin B12, and Folate.
foods.tip: Sauté with onions and black pepper once a week.

foods.name: Goat Meat / Mutton
synergies: Rich in heme iron and zinc with high Vitamin B12 content.
foods.tip: Curry or slow braised broth.

foods.name: Rohu / Freshwater Carp
synergies: Excellent source of natural Vitamin D and B12 for non-vegetarians in India.
foods.tip: Traditional mustard fish curry (Macher Jhol) or grilled fillet.

foods.name: Indian Mackerel / Bangda
synergies: Outstanding natural source of Vitamin D3 and Omega-3 fatty acids.
foods.tip: Tava fry with kokum and spices or bake.

foods.name: FSSAI Fortified Cow/Buffalo Milk (+F)
synergies: Government-mandated fortification adds 5mcg (200 IU) Vitamin D per liter.
foods.tip: Look for the blue '+F' logo on packaged Indian milk packets (Amul, Mother Dairy, Nandini).

foods.name: Fortified Soy Milk (+B12 & +Vit D)
synergies: Critical staple for strict vegans to secure bioavailable Vitamin B12 and Vitamin D without supplements.
foods.tip: Use in morning oats, tea/coffee, or smoothies.

foods.name: Fortified Nutritional Yeast Flakes
synergies: Primary non-animal gold standard for Vitamin B12 and Folate among vegans.
foods.tip: Sprinkle over popcorn, dal, pasta, or sabzis for a savory cheesy umami flavor.

foods.name: UV / Sun-Exposed Button Mushrooms
synergies: Mushrooms synthesize natural Vitamin D2 when exposed to midday sunlight for 30-60 minutes before cooking.
foods.tip: Place sliced fresh mushrooms under direct sunlight between 11 AM - 1 PM before cooking.

foods.name: Indian Gooseberry / Amla
synergies: Ultimate non-heme iron absorption booster! Contains heat-stable Vitamin C 20x higher than oranges.
foods.tip: Eat raw with a pinch of rock salt, or take 20ml fresh juice alongside morning meals.

foods.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
synergies: Ascorbic acid converts ferric iron ($Fe^{3+}$) to absorbable ferrous ($Fe^{2+}$) iron.
foods.tip: Squeeze over dal, khichdi, chana, and green vegetables right before eating.

foods.name: Ripe Guava
synergies: Exceptional whole-fruit folate and Vitamin C source.
foods.tip: Eat as a midday snack with the skin intact.

foods.name: Beetroot
synergies: High in natural dietary folate and nitrates that improve blood circulation and RBC health.
foods.tip: Grate raw into salads, juice with amla, or steam into a poriyal/thoran.

foods.name: Black Dates
synergies: Natural iron-rich sweetener for fatigue and energy support.
foods.tip: Eat 3-4 dates in the morning alongside soaked almonds.

foods.name: Almonds (Soaked & Peeled)
synergies: Healthy monounsaturated fats support absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.
foods.tip: Soak overnight in water and peel the brown skin to reduce tannins.

foods.name: Soaked Black Raisins
synergies: Traditional ayurvedic remedy for low hemoglobin and sluggish bowel transit.
foods.tip: Soak 10-12 munakkas in water overnight and consume the raisins along with the water on an empty stomach.

foods.name: Calcium-Set Firm Tofu
synergies: Calcium-sulfate setting makes tofu one of the highest plant-based calcium sources in the world.
foods.tip: Pan-fry with Indian spices or substitute for paneer in curries.

foods.name: Horse Gram
synergies: One of the richest iron-yielding legumes in the ICMR-NIN database; also high in calcium.
foods.tip: Prepare as rasam (Ulavacharu) with tamarind and tomatoes, or as a dry stir-fry.

foods.name: Moth Beans / Matki
synergies: Sprouting moth beans doubles folate content and reduces phytic acid, boosting iron absorption.
foods.tip: Sprout for 24–36 hours and prepare as misal pav or koshimbir salad.

foods.name: Cooked Soybeans
synergies: Complete plant protein; fermented forms (tempeh, miso) provide trace amounts of bioactive B12 analogues.
foods.tip: Boil and toss into chaat, curries, or dry stir-fry with spices.

foods.name: Black-Eyed Peas / Lobia
synergies: Exceptionally high in folate — one cup provides over half the adult daily requirement.
foods.tip: Make lobia curry with tomatoes and ginger-garlic, or add to salads when boiled.

foods.name: Drumstick Pods (Moringa)
synergies: Very high Vitamin C content (141 mg/100g) makes it an excellent absorption catalyst for iron-rich meals.
foods.tip: Add to sambar, dal, or pressure-cook with lentils.

foods.name: Bitter Gourd / Karela
synergies: High folate and Vitamin C; traditionally used for blood sugar management.
foods.tip: Stir-fry with onions and masalas to reduce bitterness, or stuff with spiced filling.

foods.name: Bottle Gourd / Lauki
synergies: Hydrating and easy to digest; ideal base for lentil and green-vegetable combinations.
foods.tip: Cook as lauki chana dal or lauki kofta for a nutritious combination.

foods.name: Raw Banana / Green Plantain
synergies: Resistant starch supports gut microbiome which indirectly improves mineral absorption.
foods.tip: Boil and temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and coconut; or use in Kerala-style thoran.

foods.name: Sweet Potato
synergies: Contains beta-carotene and Vitamin C; serves as a naturally sweet iron absorption co-factor.
foods.tip: Roast in the oven, boil and chaat with lemon and chilli, or mash into parathas.

foods.name: Fox Nuts / Makhana
synergies: Low-calorie, high-calcium vegan snack; a preferred fasting food in Indian households.
foods.tip: Dry roast in ghee with rock salt and black pepper as a nutritious evening snack.

foods.name: Flaxseeds / Alsi
synergies: Rich in plant omega-3 (ALA) which supports anti-inflammatory pathways aiding iron utilisation.
foods.tip: Grind and add to rotis, smoothies, or sprinkle over curd. Store ground flax in the fridge.

foods.name: Sunflower Seeds
synergies: One of the highest folate-containing seeds; also rich in Vitamin E which protects iron from oxidation.
foods.tip: Roast lightly and add to salads, granola, or trail mixes.

foods.name: Cashew Nuts
synergies: Higher iron content among common Indian nuts; copper in cashews helps iron metabolism.
foods.tip: Eat raw or lightly roasted; use in curries, kheer, or homemade barfi.

foods.name: Sorghum / Jowar
synergies: Gluten-free ancient Indian grain with moderate iron; pairs well with greens in rotlas.
foods.tip: Make jowar rotlas (thick flatbread) with garlic chutney and jaggery; also good as porridge.

foods.name: Foxtail Millet / Kangni
synergies: Richer in iron than rice; traditionally consumed in Andhra Pradesh and North India.
foods.tip: Cook as upma, pongal, or khichdi using foxtail millet instead of rice.

foods.name: Little Millet / Kutki
synergies: One of the highest iron-containing Indian millets (9.3 mg/100g dry); a traditional fasting grain.
foods.tip: Prepare as sama khichdi, sama chawal, or upma during Navratri fasting or regular meals.

foods.name: Cod Liver Oil (Supplement/Capsule)
synergies: Highly concentrated natural Vitamin D3 source; also rich in Omega-3 and preformed Vitamin A.
foods.tip: Take with a meal containing healthy fats for optimal fat-soluble vitamin absorption.

foods.name: Hilsa / Ilish Fish
synergies: Excellent B12 and Vitamin D source; widely consumed in Eastern India and Bangladesh.
foods.tip: Steamed in mustard sauce (Ilish Bhapa) or curried in mustard oil with turmeric.

foods.name: Prawns / Shrimp
synergies: Good heme iron and B12 with meaningful Vitamin D; a coastal Indian staple.
foods.tip: Prawn masala, dried prawn chutney, or prawn pulao with minimal heavy sauces.

foods.name: Mutton / Goat Liver
synergies: One of the most nutrient-dense foods on earth for iron, B12, and folate combined.
foods.tip: Stir-fry kaleja masala or add to slow-cooked biryani. Consume in moderation (once a week).

foods.name: Ripe Papaya
synergies: Contains papain enzyme which aids protein digestion and mineral assimilation; high Vitamin C catalyses iron absorption.
foods.tip: Eat fresh as a breakfast fruit, or blend into a smoothie with amla for a Vitamin C burst.

foods.name: Sweet Lime / Mosambi
synergies: Readily available Indian citrus; fresh juice squeezed over dal/iron-rich meals significantly boosts absorption.
foods.tip: Drink fresh juice (avoid packaged) immediately before or alongside iron-rich meals.

foods.name: Dried Figs / Anjeer
synergies: One of the best calcium-rich dried fruits for vegans; also provides meaningful iron.
foods.tip: Soak 2–3 anjeer in water overnight; eat the figs and drink the soaking water on an empty stomach.

foods.name: Dried Apricots / Khumani
synergies: Traditional Kashmiri and Ladakhi source of iron; pair with lemon juice for enhanced non-heme absorption.
foods.tip: Soak overnight and add to porridge, oats, or homemade trail mix.

foods.name: Desi Ghee (Clarified Butter)
synergies: Healthy saturated fat carrier; a small amount of ghee with Vitamin D-containing foods significantly enhances absorption of this fat-soluble vitamin.
foods.tip: Add 1 tsp ghee to warm dal, rice, or rotis; cook Vitamin D-containing mushrooms in ghee.

foods.name: Virgin Coconut Oil
synergies: Medium-chain triglycerides (MCTs) support absorption of fat-soluble vitamins D and B12 cofactors; use as the cooking fat when preparing Vitamin D-rich foods.
foods.tip: Use for sautéing mushrooms, fish, or eggs to maximise fat-soluble vitamin bioavailability.

foods.name: Tamarind Paste
synergies: Provides tartaric acid — an organic acid that chelates iron into a more soluble, absorbable form; a natural substitute for lemon in rasam and sambar.
foods.tip: Add to horse gram rasam, sambar, or chutneys to acidify and improve iron bioavailability.

foods.name: Jaggery / Gur (Unrefined Cane Sugar)
synergies: Traditional sweetener retaining trace minerals lost in refined sugar; iron + calcium in natural form; often paired with chana for synergistic effect.
foods.tip: Replace refined sugar with jaggery in chai, laddus, pongal, and payasam.

foods.name: Wheat Germ (Raw)
synergies: Concentrated source of folate and iron from the innermost layer of whole wheat; also rich in Vitamin E and zinc.
foods.tip: Stir 2 tbsp into curd, smoothies, or breakfast upma for a quick folate boost.

foods.name: Tempeh (Fermented Soybean Cake)
synergies: Fermentation breaks down phytic acid, making iron and calcium more bioavailable than unfermented soy. Provides trace amounts of B12 analogues.
foods.tip: Marinate in Indian spices (turmeric, chilli, coriander) and pan-fry or bake as a protein-rich side.
